judge_summary: All five active requirements fail because the patch changes contributor/CI documentation only and does not update the required maintained installation or authentication guidance. No deduction-only guardrail is violated.

Fails multiple P0 requirements (C1, C2, C4, and C5), so the patch is non-mergeable under the rubric. It provides usable Argo recovery context but lacks the required CRD, hard-affinity, and complete resource-output documentation.

The patch updates the primary recovery documentation with a valid image retrieval-and-patch sequence, but it does not require both fields, retrieve the rollout-request status value, or explain the later-rollout consequence of leaving the attempted image in spec.

The patch adds useful CDC basics and a prominent WAL-retention warning, but it misses multiple P0 requirements, including scheduled-sync coverage, permission correction, complete prerequisites, and publication-mode responsibilities.
Fails C4, C9, C11, C12, C15, C16, and C19. C2 passes; no P0 deduction-only violation is present.
C1 blocks mergeability: the patch directs external-feature-flag users to manually emit `$feature_flag_called` instead of documenting the required custom-exposure workflow.

Fails the P0 multi-schema requirement because Supabase is not updated. It also misses or contradicts several column-selection, resync, Supabase-discovery, metadata-recovery, and selection-state requirements.
Fails C3, C7, C8, C9, and C19. C3 and C7 are P0 requirement failures, so the patch is non-mergeable.

The patch documents funnel path-cleaning support and global-rule activation, but lacks precise URL/pathname scope, a reader-benefit explanation, separate funnel point-of-use coverage, a configuration link, UI-label formatting, and a concrete alias example.

The patch adds limited retry-predicate prose but does not implement the required PyFlink Async I/O guide, examples, timeout guidance, API reference, or navigation. It also inaccurately presents `exception_type_predicate` as directly usable.

The patch adds general key-mismatch prose outside the INSERT reference but omits all required ON CONFLICT syntax, behavior, configuration, examples, and links. It also introduces an unsupported last-record-wins guarantee, violating the P0 guardrail.

Fails the required HMS positional-validation, configuration, scope, operation-family, deployment, trade-off, and Spark/Flink journey criteria. C9 is violated by an unsupported promise that Hive commands update both definitions together.
No change was needed; official decision score is zero

The canonical documentation gains a focused semicolon example, but it incorrectly promises verbatim preservation of a physical line rather than defining same-logical-line statement suppression. This causes C1, C8, C11, and C14 failures.
The patch adds reverse-proxy and basic metrics-hook material, but retains central stale claims and omits most required port, migration, health, troubleshooting, verification, and limitation details.

The patch adds a valid public API section with context-relative paths and chaining, but omits the core early dependency-install behavior, dependency-install workflow, in-image lifetime, wheels behavior, and troubleshooting coverage.
C1 and C7 pass. C4 fails due to a strict processing-order claim; canonical configuration and API updates, cross-references, rationale, and discoverability requirements are missing.

The patch adds useful display-name syntax and fallback documentation, but misses Graphviz scope, programmatic-operation guidance, tag-reference coverage, and a runnable example with matching graph. It also breaks the surrounding RST section structure and misrepresents applicability to input nodes.

The patch adds a clear, inspectable pre-load add_map example and overview route, but omits most required API, ordering, cursor, type-semantics, operational, and integration coverage; the new page is also not registered in the sidebar.

The AWS material is structurally clear but non-mergeable: all three setup examples use the incorrect generic `rest` catalog selector, omit required AWS credential/region configuration, and the patch leaves the stale two-catalog overview unaddressed. It also lacks the required AWS setup links.

The patch correctly makes the request source conditional and documents local/remote definitions and mock behavior, but it lacks the required user-facing guide, reusable-context coverage, generator source changes, navigation, and several required reference details.
No change was needed; official decision score is zero

Fails core completeness and integration requirements: the patch adds isolated schema references but omits test/action guidance, navigation, generation metadata, synchronized affected references, and required examples. It also incorrectly claims omitted `language` runs in the shell.
The patch supplies a valid multi-input command and purpose explanation, but fails C1 because it does not document the `-i` alias.
The patch is a clear, non-behavioral typo correction that preserves the existing documentation coverage and table structure.

The patch adds useful issue-mediated AI-triage documentation on the correct public pages, but lacks an actionable prompt-bearing configuration example, maintainer-use rationale, prompt-crafting guidance, a complete scheduled example, invalid-integration troubleshooting, and a named prerequisite setup link.
The patch documents automatic default loading clearly, but omits alternate-file selection, selected-configuration path semantics, an updated supporting sample, and a concrete invocation comparison.

The patch directly edits a generated schema reference and removes an unrelated default example, but does not document the requested remote-input or detected-test workflows. C8 and the triggered style criterion fail; no deduction-only prohibited content is introduced.
Fails P0 criteria C2 and C4; the patch is not mergeable. It also lacks the HTTPS exception and inline tests, and includes prohibited Docker guidance.
Passes C1, C2, C6, C8, C11, C14, and C16. Fails C4, C5, C7, and C12; C13 and C15 are not triggered; neither deduction-only guardrail is violated.

Fails the core Podinfo repair and Helm 3 parity requirements. It also falsely claims direct OCI registry search and leaves an unqualified dynamic deployment timestamp.

Both primary workflows and compatibility reconciliation are present, but the patch lacks dependency guidance, CLI storage-dtype documentation, the FSDP checkpoint caveat, dtype tradeoffs, and added resource-planning/deeper-reference value. C4 and C1 pass; no P0 failure is present.

The patch modernizes portions of the package README initialization snippets, but it omits the required primary Java documentation path and nearly all required workflows. Its VPC-only Enterprise wording also violates the endpoint-scope guardrail.

It also incorrectly claims automatic registered-name resolution for handler objects.

Passes the core default web-root guidance and its placement, but fails to update the stale custom-root version constraint, omits the required public-folder server-root instruction, and adds an unresolved cross-reference.
Passes the core cron-safety requirements, but fails RST shell highlighting, the adjacent queued-delivery improvement, and the triggered time-limit current-message explanation.

Fails multiple blocking P0 requirements (C2, C3, C4, and C5) and violates the blocking P0 accelerator-behavior safeguard (C8).

The patch adds a concise optional Price Sheet variable overview in the appropriate Azure documentation page, but it omits most of the required setup, permissions, deployment, behavior, verification, troubleshooting, and limitation documentation.

The patch adds Grafana-oriented historical workload examples, but it lacks the required four-component 30-day namespace-and-type query, control guidance, exclusions, and working cross-reference. It also makes an unqualified OpenCost UI parity claim.
